Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the MediCore Health Systems second quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss MediCore Health Systems' financial results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lisa Chen, Chief Medical Officer; and Karen Patel, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our strong performance for the second quarter of 2024. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network through targeted acquisitions and partnerships, and improving operational efficiency across our system.

Today, I'll provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, highlighting the impact of our recent acquisitions, the benefits from our value-based care initiatives, volume trends in admissions and patient days, factors driving our operating margin performance, and the status of our ongoing and planned M&A activities. These elements underscore our resilience in a dynamic healthcare landscape marked by shifting reimbursement models, population growth in key markets, and the ongoing transition to outpatient and value-based services.

Let me start with our volume metrics, which formed a solid foundation for the quarter. Total admissions reached 52,400 across our expanded network, reflecting a 15.8% increase year-over-year from 45,200 in the prior-year period and an 8.3% sequential improvement from 48,300 in the first quarter. Patient days totaled 291,200, up 16.1% year-over-year from 250,700 and 9.4% quarter-over-quarter from 266,100. These gains were propelled by a rebound in elective procedures, now at 42% of our mix, including orthopedics and cardiology interventions like TAVR. Our case mix index improved to 1.85, up 4.2% year-over-year, supporting higher reimbursements. Average length of stay held steady at 5.56 days, with readmission rates at 14.2%, outperforming national benchmarks. Regionally, our Southeast facilities led with 18% admission growth, aided by commercial payer strength and demographic tailwinds, while Midwest markets grew 12% despite softer industrial demand.

These volumes, combined with payer mix improvements, set the stage for revenue momentum. Now, I'll turn the call over to Tom to walk through our financial results in greater detail, including the contributions from recent acquisitions, value-based care dynamics, margin drivers, and our M&A pipeline.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Michael, and good morning, everyone. As Michael noted, we delivered a solid quarter. Net revenue for the second quarter came in at $4.8 billion, an 18% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by higher patient volumes, favorable payer shifts, and the integration of key acquisitions.

Let me first address the transformative impact of our two major acquisitions over the past 12 months: the $1.2 billion purchase of Southeast Regional Hospitals in the third quarter of 2023, adding 1,800 licensed beds across 12 facilities in Florida, Georgia, and the Carolinas; and the $850 million acquisition of Apex Outpatient Partners in the first quarter of 2024, which included 45 ambulatory surgery centers and 20 urgent care clinics mainly in Texas and Arizona. These $2.1 billion deals were funded with $1.4 billion from our balance sheet, supported by robust free cash flow, and $700 million in term debt at an average 4.2% rate.

Pro forma, these assets contributed $650 million, or 14% of total revenue. Organically, revenue grew 7%, with patient days up 5% and net revenue per admission rising 2% to $14,200, thanks to more commercial patients and Medicare Advantage at 42%. SRH generated $420 million in run-rate revenue, beating expectations by 8%, especially in Florida where inpatient utilization jumped 12% from post-COVID demand and 2.5% annual population growth. AOP added $230 million, with 15% same-facility growth in orthopedics and gastroenterology, average revenue per case at $3,800 up 6%, bolstered by bundled contracts with UnitedHealthcare and Cigna representing 28% of mix. Texas saw 22% volume increases in Dallas-Fort Worth due to Medicaid expansions.

On profitability, adjusted EBITDA hit $1.05 billion, up 22% year-over-year, with margins expanding 140 basis points to 22.1%. SRH added $185 million at 44% margins, driven by high-acuity cardiology and oncology with a CMI of 2.05. We've captured $45 million in run-rate synergies from SRH, including $25 million from Vizient GPO supply chain savings cutting implant costs 12%, and $20 million from RCM consolidation. AOP contributed $95 million at 41% margins, with $18 million synergies from Epic integration at 85% complete and admin staff optimization. Total synergies reached $63 million in the first half, tracking to $150 million for the year, with cross-referrals boosting SRH admissions 25% and adding $12 million in revenue. Diluted EPS rose 19% to $2.45, with acquisitions adding 24 cents; non-GAAP accretion was 15%. Leverage improved to 3.1x, ROIC at 12.5% scaling to 15% by 2026.

Strategically, these moves advance our value-based care position, with SRH enhancing ACO REACH for 1.2 million lives and $35 million in H1 shared savings. AI analytics from Oracle Health reduced SRH LOS by 0.4 days to 4.2, adding 50 basis points to margins. AOP's telehealth urgent cares saw 40% virtual visit growth to 15,000 monthly, targeting MA growth. Sunbelt demographics provide tailwinds, and we've offset CMS's 2.9% IPPS cut with 4.1% commercial increases.

Turning to our value-based care contracts, which now represent 28% of net patient revenue—up from 18% last year—they generated $1.2 billion in Q2, growing 32% year-over-year and outpacing overall revenue. Mature programs like our Track 3 MSSP ACO for 250,000 lives delivered 8-12% reimbursement uplifts per episode. In joint bundles under CJR 2.0, we hit $18,200 per case, including $2,800 in post-acute savings from 15% readmission reductions via CarePathway, integrating Epic with Cerner and Google Cloud AI. Southeast markets like Atlanta and Jacksonville benefited from 45% Medicare FFS and 22% MA penetration, with Florida ACO REACH yielding $45 million in H1 savings from 22% lower SNF use. Margins expanded 250 basis points to 18.5%. Midwest VBC is at 15%, with hybrid contracts preserving $28 million amid COPD pressures.

We've invested $75 million in VBC infrastructure, including FHIR interoperability and our Quality Engine, boosting RAF scores 12% and adding $120 million in MA coding. Medical loss ratio is 92%, yielding $180 million YTD savings. Headwinds like CMS benchmark adjustments were offset by 11% cost reductions via home health stakes and 85/15 risk splits. We expect VBC at 35% of revenue by 2025, adding $300-350 million EBITDA.

Operating expenses were $3.67 billion, or about 76.5% of net revenue, as we managed costs tightly while investing in growth. Our operating margin reached 13.2%, up 110 basis points year-over-year. Revenue grew 9.2% to $2.85 billion on 6.8% admission increases to 145,000, CMI to 1.92, and 14.5% outpatient surge from three new ASCs. Commercial mix at 55%, NRPA up 2.1% to $21,450, denials down to 4.2%.

Expenses rose 6.8% to $2.47 billion. Labor, 52% of costs, increased 5.2% via reduced contract labor to 8%, Talent Pipeline filling 1,200 roles, and AI scheduling cutting overtime 18%. Supplies up 7.1% to $425 million, saved via 340B at 85% facilities ($120 million), 9% implant reductions through HealthTrust. Bad debt at 2.8%. Urban margins at 15.1%, rural 10.8%; telehealth cut ALOS 0.4 days. Bundled ortho partnerships and Cerner upgrades support Q3 margins of 13.5-14.0%.

Finally, on M&A, our strategy emphasizes Sun Belt densification, vertical integration, and optimization. Ongoing: $650 million Coastal Care Network closed September, adding 1,450 beds, 58% commercial mix, $25 million synergies from HealthTrust GPO and R1 RCM; Epic 85% live, psych utilization 92%. Pending: $425 million Midwest Behavioral Health, eight psych facilities, $18 million synergies from telepsych. Divestitures: $210 million for five rural CAHs at 1.2x capital, proceeds for repurchases. Pipeline: $300 million Texas ASCs, $150 million Florida home health. YTD divestitures $320 million keep leverage at 3.1x. Oracle Health unlocks $40 million savings.

Net income was $450 million, or $2.45 per diluted share. Operating cash flow was $450 million. We're confident in our full-year outlook.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Chen for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Tom. Good morning. We're advancing clinical outcomes and satisfaction. Our CarePathway program reduced readmissions 15%, to 6.1% in bundles. Leveraging Epic, Cerner AI, and telehealth, we've improved coordination, with virtual visits up 40%. Our ACO efforts maintain 95% STAR ratings in MA, supporting quality incentives.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Michael.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Lisa. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from David Miller with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Miller:
Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the impact of the recent acquisitions like SRH and AOP on your revenue growth and their effect on hospital efficiency?

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Good morning, David. Absolutely. As Tom detailed, SRH and AOP drove 14% of our revenue, with SRH exceeding underwriting by 8% on surgical volumes and AOP accelerating outpatient shift with 15% same-facility growth. Efficiency-wise, synergies like supply chain savings and Epic integration have boosted EBITDA margins above system averages—44% for SRH, 41% for AOP—while cross-referrals increased admissions 25%. AI analytics cut LOS, enhancing throughput at 82% utilization.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Thanks. What are your plans for expanding your network of hospitals and clinics in the coming year?

Karen Patel:
Hi, Emily. We're focused on bolt-ons like Coastal Care for Southeast density and behavioral health via Midwest Behavioral to address shortages. Divesting low-margin rurals recycles capital into ASCs and home health, targeting 5-7% organic growth. Sun Belt priorities leverage MA hotspots and demographics for 12-14% revenue expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kline with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline:
Can you elaborate on the specific technologies you are implementing to improve care coordination?

Dr. Lisa Chen:
Sure, Robert. Our stack includes Epic MyChart with AI predictive analytics, live in 85% of sites, reducing no-shows 22% and optimizing discharges. CarePathway integrates EHR with Cerner and Google Cloud for risk stratification, cutting readmissions 15-22%. Telepsych and eICU from Philips handle 25% consults, lowering staffing needs while boosting VBC savings.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Thompson with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Laura Thompson:
On margins, how sustainable is the 13.2% with labor and supply pressures?

Tom Hargrove:
Laura, thanks. Sustainability comes from revenue quality—CMI gains, payer mix—and controls like 340B expansion, GPO negotiations, and AI scheduling. Regional strategies differentiate urban premium from rural Medicare, with VBC and bundles adding leverage. Q3 guide 13.5-14.0% assumes steady volumes.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes the question-and-answer session. I'll now turn the call back over to Dr. Reynolds for closing remarks.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the MediCore Health Systems second quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
